extracted.intended_audience: authors/aspiring writers seeking to submit manuscripts to Pan Macmillan Australia (traditional publishing applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and practical criteria for direct manuscript submissions to Pan Macmillan Australia: which genres they seek, what materials/files to send, how to submit, and a short readiness checklist (revisions, beta readers, agreement to guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction genres sought
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction: Contemporary drama, sagas, psychological suspense, crime and thrillers, historical, literary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists these specific fiction subgenres as what Pan Macmillan Australia is currently seeking (i.e., preferred submissions should fit one of these categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction genres sought
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-fiction: Narrative non-fiction, contemporary issues, memoir, history, true crime, lifestyle and health, mind body spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions of non-fiction should align with these narrative and topical areas the imprint has identified as of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's & Young Adult genres sought
rubrics_metrics.description: Children’s books & young adult fiction: Junior and middle grade fiction, young adult/crossover fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts for children’s and YA markets should target the stated age bands and crossover YA where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission window / availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Pan Macmillan Australia are now open to submissions year round (they used to be open only the first Monday of every month).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may submit at any time; the submission form is accessible and no longer restricted to a monthly opening day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required materials — manuscript sample and synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: They ask that you send the first 50 pages of your manuscript along with a synopsis that is no more than 300 words in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both items should be prepared before submission; synopsis must not exceed 300 words. The guideline emphasises submitting only the requested excerpt length rather than a full manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: File formats and document separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit the manuscript pages and the synopsis as separate Word or PDF documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send each required item as its own .doc/.docx or .pdf file (i.e., do not combine synopsis and sample into one file).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple manuscripts policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You can submit multiple manuscripts as long as they are not in the same series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher allows multiple distinct manuscripts from the same author but disallows sending several books that are installments of the same series in simultaneous submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method — use the submission manager
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions are made through their easy to use submission manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must submit via Pan Macmillan Australia's online submission manager (the page provides a link to learn more). Submissions sent by other channels are not described as acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of additional form questions
rubrics_metrics.description: They have additional questions outlined on their form, and you can see and review the questions at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and answer extra metadata/questions on the publisher's submission form; the form and its questions are available even when submissions are open or closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript readiness — revise at least three times
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you revised your manuscript at least 3 times? (The short pre-submission form asks this question.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are urged to revise their work multiple times before submitting; the site links to resources about revising a manuscript. This is presented as a gate/expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek beta reader feedback before submitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you gotten beta reader feedback? (The pre-submission form asks whether you've received beta reader feedback.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher (via this guidance page) encourages authors to obtain external reader feedback prior to submission and links to information about the importance of beta readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to study publisher's guidelines and catalog
rubrics_metrics.description: I agree to only submit after carefully studying the publisher's guidelines and catalog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are asked to confirm they will study Pan Macmillan Australia's submission guidelines and catalogue before sending work; this acts as a consent/acknowledgement step on the pre-submission form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid submitting unpolished or inappropriate work (consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting to un-polished or inappropriate work can ruin your reputation and can (and has) cause a publisher to close submissions to everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a warning/anti-pattern: poor-quality or unsuited submissions harm both the individual and the wider writing community. The page links to guidance on how to appropriately submit a book to avoid this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pan Macmillan Australia is the direct route to Macmillan
rubrics_metrics.description: Pan Macmillan Australia are the Australian imprint of Macmillan, one of the big five publishers. This is the only way to submit to Macmillan directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual note: authors wanting to submit directly to Macmillan in Australia should use this imprint's submission channel.
